helperIds.lastFourTokenCensor: Returns a deterministic token derived from the final four characters of the original value.
helperIds.stableEnvelopeSerialiser: Serialises the redacted value inside a deterministic fixture envelope.

migrationSteps: Keep the dot-path selector unchanged.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: With serialize: false, fast-redact returns the redacted object for the configured dot path.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 returns the same structured redacted object for the same selector.
v4Action.reason: The selector syntax and structured result are equivalent.

migrationSteps: Keep the bracket-quoted property selector unchanged.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: fast-redact targets the quoted property name exactly.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 targets the same quoted property name exactly.
v4Action.reason: The quoted property path syntax is shared.

migrationSteps: Keep the numeric array-index selector unchanged.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: fast-redact redacts the selected array element only.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 redacts the same array element only.
v4Action.reason: Numeric bracket indexes have the same migration meaning.

migrationSteps: Keep the final-position wildcard selector unchanged.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: fast-redact redacts every immediate child matched by the final wildcard.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 redacts the same immediate children.
v4Action.reason: Final-position wildcard targeting is equivalent for this documented shape.

migrationSteps: Keep the intermediate wildcard selector unchanged.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: fast-redact redacts matching descendants beneath each wildcard segment.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 redacts the same descendant values.
v4Action.reason: The shared wildcard string syntax is accepted by both libraries.

migrationSteps: Keep the leading bracket-quoted property selector unchanged.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: fast-redact accepts a leading bracket-quoted property selector and redacts the selected descendant.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 accepts the same leading bracket-quoted property selector and redacts the selected descendant.
v4Action.reason: The leading bracket-quoted property path syntax is shared.

migrationSteps: Keep the literal string censor unchanged.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: fast-redact replaces the selected value with the configured string.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 replaces the selected value with the same string.
v4Action.reason: String censors are supported by both libraries.

migrationSteps: Keep the function censor intent and map it to a declared Deep Redact v4 function.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: fast-redact calls the configured censor function for the selected value.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 calls the equivalent configured censor function for the selected value.
v4Action.reason: The fixture helper proves compatible one-argument censor behaviour without embedding source code in JSON.

migrationSteps: Rewrite the bracket array wildcard path from `accounts[*].secret` to `accounts.*.secret`.
Omit serialise for structured Deep Redact v4 output.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: fast-redact accepts bracket array wildcard syntax.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 accepts the equivalent dot wildcard syntax.
v4Action.reason: Deep Redact v4 rejects bracket wildcard syntax, so the selector needs a mechanical path rewrite.

migrationSteps: Rename `serialize` to `serialise`.
Keep the explicit false value when preserving structured output intent.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 uses the British-English `serialise` option.
v4Action.reason: The output intent is the same, but the public option spelling changes.

migrationSteps: Set `serialise: true` when the old `fast-redact` call relied on default JSON string output.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: fast-redact serialises with JSON.stringify by default.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 returns structured output by default, so JSON string output must be requested explicitly.
v4Action.reason: The default output type changed and needs an explicit option in migrated code.

migrationSteps: Rename `serialize` to `serialise`.
Move the existing custom serialiser function to the Deep Redact v4 option.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: fast-redact passes the redacted value to the configured serialize function.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 passes the redacted value to the configured serialise function.
v4Action.reason: The serialiser function role is equivalent after the option is renamed.

migrationSteps: Keep `remove: true`.
Set `serialise: true` because fast-redact remove output is tied to JSON serialisation.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: fast-redact removes the selected property from its default JSON string output.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 removes the selected property and serialises when `serialise: true` is set.
v4Action.reason: Removal intent is equivalent, but migrated code must request serialisation explicitly.

migrationSteps: Do not migrate code that calls `restore` to an equivalent Deep Redact v4 API.
Keep an unredacted source value separately if application logic still needs it.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: With serialize: false, fast-redact exposes a redactor.restore method for caller-side reversal.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 redactors expose no restore, unredact, or reverse-operation method.
v4Action.reason: Deep Redact v4 is intentionally one-way.

migrationSteps: Remove `strict` from the Deep Redact v4 configuration.
Handle primitive inputs according to the migrated caller's policy before calling Deep Redact v4.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: With strict: false and serialize: false, fast-redact returns the primitive input unchanged when the redactor sees a primitive instead of an object.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 rejects the unsupported `strict` option during initialisation.
v4Action.reason: Deep Redact v4 does not provide a strict compatibility switch for primitive input handling.

migrationSteps: Set `serialise: true` in Deep Redact v4 if the old call depended on the fast-redact default JSON string.
Leave `serialise` omitted only when the migrated caller wants structured output.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: fast-redact returns a JSON string when `serialize` is omitted.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 returns structured output when `serialise` is omitted.
v4Action.reason: The default output type intentionally differs.

migrationSteps: Replace non-string literal censors with a string censor or a function censor before migrating.
Use a function censor if the migrated code needs to return a non-string value deliberately.
v4Action.fastRedactBehaviour: fast-redact accepts documented non-string censor values such as number literals.
v4Action.v4Behaviour: Deep Redact v4 rejects root censor values that are neither strings nor functions.
v4Action.reason: The v4 public Censor contract is intentionally narrower.
